notes: AHRQ Effective Health Care Methods Guide page was live and reread on 2026-08-27.
NIH/NLM PubMed and PubMed Central methods literature was reread for stable diagnostic-accuracy bias definitions; a 2022 dedicated partial-verification methods paper directly supports the core claim.

claim_audit.correct_mechanism: The NLM/PubMed 2022 methods paper states that partial verification bias occurs when a positive index test makes application of the reference standard more likely. The NLM/PMC diagnostic-accuracy review defines it as a nonrandom set of tested patients not undergoing the reference standard.
claim_audit.classical_design: AHRQ describes the classical diagnostic-accuracy paradigm as comparing the index test with reference/true status for every tested individual and notes verification bias when reference-standard use is guided by the index result.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NLM/PMC defines spectrum bias as arising when the included patient spectrum does not represent the intended target population. Consecutive clinically relevant enrollment in the stem removes that defining defect.
claim_audit.distractor_2: NLM/PMC defines differential verification bias as using different reference standards for different participants. The stem explicitly specifies one reference standard—coronary angiography.
claim_audit.distractor_3: NLM/PMC defines incorporation bias as including the index test in the reference standard. The stem explicitly keeps angiography independent of the blood test.
claim_audit.distractor_4: NLM/PMC defines reference-standard review/information bias as interpretation of the reference standard with knowledge of the index result. The angiographers are explicitly blinded.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: All participants receive the index test, but verification of disease status by the single reference standard is much more likely after a positive index result. Diagnostic accuracy is then calculated only in the selectively verified subset. This is precisely partial verification/workup bias.
adversarial_second_pass.spectrum_challenge: The study enrolls consecutive adults in the intended clinical population; no extreme-case/control sampling or restricted disease spectrum is described.
adversarial_second_pass.differential_verification_challenge: Different reference standards are not used. A single standard is selectively applied, which distinguishes partial from differential verification.
adversarial_second_pass.incorporation_challenge: The index test does not contribute to the angiographic definition of disease.
adversarial_second_pass.review_bias_challenge: Reference-standard interpreters are blinded to the index-test result, removing the defining review-bias mechanism.
adversarial_second_pass.sampling_fraction_challenge: A random fraction of index-negative participants is verified, but the naïve analysis is restricted to verified participants without sampling-fraction correction; selective verification therefore remains the design defect.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No exact numerical distortion of sensitivity or specificity is asserted in the question or required for the answer.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are named diagnostic-accuracy biases and are comparable in length and abstraction level.
